title: Admit explicit recording intent and nonwriting preview requests
statement: The Command handling Module shall admit explicit bounded task intent and preserve its authority, scope and preview/execution distinction.

what.problem: Defaulting actor decisions or changing scope can undermine explicit recording intent.
what.desired_outcome: The persistence boundary receives one unambiguous bounded semantic task with its declared basis and preview intent.

why.rationale: SR-043 requires explicit semantic inputs and equivalent nonwriting preview; MOD-010 owns their public admission and outcome meaning while MOD-011 constructs candidates.

stakeholders: Engineers and agents supplying explicit command requests
Maintainers of MOD-010 and its Interface consumers

conditions: A caller invokes a supported task mutation or its nonwriting preview.

contexts: IF-004 recording admission and the IF-003 construction, preview, and publication handoff.

how.approach: Apply the current v4 SQLite task and maintenance contract. Require explicit semantic task values, project/Change/item scope and current revision; missing or unknown input rejects without invented decisions.

how_much.scope: This allocation preserves its existing parent SR and accountable Module. Prior v3 file-journal mechanisms are historical at 39be9c81; current maintenance remains separately explicit.

acceptance_criteria: Require explicit semantic task values, project/Change/item scope and current revision; missing or unknown input rejects without invented decisions.
Creation selects an unused Change ID and explicit request/authority; it does not require or infer prior requirement/design approval.
Admit one bounded task with its related typed facts. Review assessment, evidence, issue disposition and completion remain distinct semantic operations.
Preview and execution use the same closed input definitions; preview makes no reservation and actual execution repeats freshness checks.
No legacy advanced replacement or arbitrary batch command survives. Skills use the public task contract without SQL or runtime-file reconstruction.
constraints: Current v4 SQLite realization; source observations do not establish engineering approval or passing implementation proof.

sources.basis: Derive this draft lower-level obligation from the containing SR at the selected command or operational-record responsibility boundary. Allocation and acceptance criteria are design claims for review, not implementation, requirement approval, or satisfaction evidence.

sources.locator: docs/design/cli/cli.md#CLI-SR-03, CLI-SR-12, CLI-SR-15, CLI-SR-16, CLI-SR-25, CLI-SR-26; docs/design/cli/records.md#RF-SR-02, RF-SR-03
sources.basis: Preserve the applicable current public and stored-record guarantees at this accountable boundary. The named source retains exact schemas, operation tables, classifications, limits, and historical adoption obligations; this allocation neither replaces those details nor accepts REM authoring JSON as operational records.

Reconcile the existing allocation with refined SR-042–044 and the explicit v4/v2 contract. Keep current-v3 byte and mutation guarantees version-scoped, preserve historical originals, and distinguish precommit recovery from committed outcome reporting. This target allocation is not runtime qualification.
Refine existing current-state responsibility and selective retention; observed runtime mappings remain version-scoped.

sources.locator: docs/design/cli/records.md; Work records (MOD-011) current transaction and maintenance contract
sources.basis: Reconciles existing stakeholder need and allocation with SQLite ordinary recovery. No new need, approval, or executed result is inferred.
